note: A single shaded site in woods at the end of a long back-in gravel driveway, an old haul road, on the south side of Licking Creek Drive about 0.2 mile east of Camp Saratoga. The booking page sells it as a trailer site; DCNR's 2022 campsite map layer lists it as having no trailer access. Picnic table and stone fire ring; no toilet or water. Pack out trash. --Claude
summary: Site page re-read: 017 still listed and bookable online, Drive-In, Horse/Tent/Trailer categories, max vehicle and equipment length 25 ft, back-in gravel driveway 200 ft, grades Slight, clearance 15 ft, picnic table; count 1 and 25 ft confirmed, pull_through false and a sites note added. Year-round confirmed; sells in all five windows. Fees confirmed, $6.50 reservation fee added; hookups and facilities none. Imagery (Esri leaf-on: closed canopy; PASDA leaf-off: bare woods): the pin is about 60 m from the forest road, which fits the 200-ft driveway; no pad can be made out. NHD: West Licking Creek 140 m away; not waterfront.
flags: ROAD / NAME: '(North Block)' is only the booking system's loop label. The page puts site 017 'on Licking Creek Drive, about 0.2 mile east of Camp Saratoga. Site on south side of road' (the GIS notes say the same and call the driveway an 'Old haul road'). Note the page for 013 says 'East Licking Creek Drive' and this one 'Licking Creek Drive'; each is quoted as written. Suggested name: 'Tuscarora State Forest Campsite 017 (Licking Creek Drive)'. apply.py does not write names.

DCNR MAP LAYER vs BOOKING PAGE (ruling 5, reported not asked): the DCNR Designated Campsites layer (record last edited 2022-12-20) says 'TrailerAccess: No' for site 017; the booking page sells it with 'Looking For Category: Horse Site, Tent Site, Trailer Site' and 'Max Vehicle Length: 25'. Kept; both statements are in the note.

EQUIPMENT (rulings 4 and 8, reported not raised): the page lists 'Looking For Category: Horse Site, Tent Site, Trailer Site' with no 'RV Site' category; Max Vehicle Length 25, Site Access Drive-In. Kept.

Back-in only: 'Driveway Entry: Back-In', 'Driveway Length: 200' on an old haul road. The agency says nothing against it; reported so the owner knows a 200-ft reverse is involved (or a turn at the pad, which imagery cannot show under the trees).
Overhead: 'Site Height/Overhead Clearance: 15', 'Shade: Shaded'; imagery is closed canopy. 15 ft is over the 10.5-ft line; nothing to act on.

Agency access statements (ruling 11: nothing measured, no road surface, gate or bridge research): 'Site Grade: Slight', 'Driveway Grade: Slight', gravel. No caution line. The page also carries the district-wide 'Road and Travel Alert' and '4WD vehicles may be recommended for some sites year-round, check notes' boilerplate (this site's notes say nothing about 4WD).
Ground: no pad identified under canopy or on leaf-off imagery; the pin stays on the agency point (page and GIS agree).
Water: NHD has West Licking Creek 140 m from the site, woods between; not waterfront, no lead.

Tuscarora advisories page (read 2026-11-10): district office construction (mid-July to early November 2025), a chronic wasting disease notice, firewood. No road closure, gate, bridge limit or timber-sale notice. The Tuscarora camping page publishes no seasonal closure or site rotation; it says only 'State forest roads do not receive winter maintenance and are not plowed --motorized, roadside camping access is not guaranteed. Travel at your own risk.' It names one equestrian area, Showaker; this site is not in it.
